findings.title: Negative offsets bypass pagination bounds in OptimizedCursorPaginator
findings.body: With enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0, the code slices queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start. Django QuerySets raise AssertionError on negative indexing/slicing, so a crafted cursor such as `0:-5:1` gives a 500 error. The comment claiming Django handles this is wrong. The `Cursor.from_string` path accepts negative offsets from user input, and the feature is gated only by a user-controllable query param.

findings.title: BasePaginator now passes negative offsets to the queryset for prev cursors
findings.body: Changing the slice to `start_offset = offset if cursor.is_prev` lets negative offsets reach `queryset[...]` for every paginator subclass. Previously a negative offset also failed, but now it is deliberately preserved, and the `stop` computation changes. A user-supplied prev cursor with a negative offset can trigger an assertion error or unexpected results across all endpoints that use BasePaginator. The later `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check also uses the unclamped offset.

findings.title: Unrelated, weakly justified paginator path on audit log endpoint
findings.body: The audit log endpoint adds an opt-in `optimized_pagination` mode that exposes the negative-offset code to superusers and global-access members. This is unrelated to the spans buffer change described in the PR. `organization_context.member` may be None for superusers who are not members, which would raise AttributeError. Trailing whitespace is also present.

findings.title: Redirect depth limit reduced from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: The loop bound dropped from 10000 to 1000 with no explanation. Segment trees deeper than 1000 will no longer be joined correctly, which regresses behavior the old comment documented.

findings.title: Removed max_segment_spans check; the limit is now enforced only in Lua
findings.body: The span-count guard in _load_segment_data was removed, and `max_segment_spans` is now unused. The Lua script hard-codes 1000 and evicts the lowest-scored entries via zpopmin. The two limits are inconsistent (the config default is 1001), and the config is no longer honored. Spans are silently dropped without a metric.

findings.title: end_timestamp_precise accessed as a required key
findings.body: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises KeyError if a span lacks the field. That crashes the whole batch in the consumer. Using `.get` with a fallback, or dropping the span, would be safer.
